title: Group 1s and 2s, Min Swaps
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers, each `0`, `1` or `2`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the minimum total cost.

examples.explanation: Swap the middle pair (2, 1) to get 1 1 2 2, which is grouped. That costs 1. Making 2s come first would need 3 swaps, so the answer is 1.

Ignoring zeros the order of the other values is 2 1 2 1. Zeros move for free, so only the relative order of 1s and 2s costs anything. One swap of the middle pair gives 2 2 1 1, and the 0s can be slid to the ends at no cost.
There is no 1 at all, so the 2s only need to be contiguous, and they already are after free moves of the 0.

hints: Zeros are free to move, so delete them mentally. Only the relative order of the 1s and 2s matters, and only a swap of an adjacent 1 and 2 costs anything.
In the sequence of 1s and 2s, you must end with either all 1s before all 2s or all 2s before all 1s. Each adjacent 1-2 swap fixes exactly one out-of-order pair.
Count the pairs (1 before 2) and the pairs (2 before 1) with a single left-to-right scan. The answer is the smaller of the two counts.
